intro.title: Image Lazy Loading
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React component that efficiently loads images only when they are about to appear in the user's viewport, a technique known as lazy loading. You will learn the core concept of conditionally rendering content based on element visibility using the browser's Intersection Observer API. The main technologies involved are React functional components with TypeScript, the `useRef` and `useState` hooks for managing state and references, and the Intersection Observer for detecting visibility. By the end, you'll create a reusable `LazyImage` component that improves your app's performance by reducing initial page load time.
intro.usecase: Image lazy loading is essential for performance in content-heavy applications like e-commerce product galleries, social media feeds, and news/article websites. When users scroll through Instagram's infinite feed or browse Amazon's product listings, images load only as they enter the viewport, reducing initial page weight and improving load times. Developers implement this pattern in dashboards with data visualizations, portfolio sites with image grids, and any UI where numerous images could impact Core Web Vitals like Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).
